messages.content: Write a short announcement for a new feature in a note-taking app: offline sync. Around 200 words.

output:
Clean through the slopwatch gate. 201 words:

## Offline sync

Offline sync is live on desktop, iOS, and Android as of today.

Until now, notes you wrote without a connection stayed on the device that made them. Open the app on your laptop after a flight and yesterday's scribbles were still on your phone. Edit the same note in two places and you got a second copy with "conflict" in the title.

That changes with this release. Every edit made offline is written to a local log and replayed against the server when you reconnect. Edits to different parts of a note merge on their own. When two people genuinely change the same paragraph, we keep both versions and show them side by side so you pick, rather than guessing for you and burying the loser in a duplicate file.

The sync queue survives a force-quit and a reboot. There is nothing to turn on and no separate offline mode to remember to enter, though you can watch the queue drain from the status dot in the sidebar if you want to.

Notebooks over 2 GB sync their most recent 90 days first, then backfill. We are working on making that window configurable.

Bug reports go to support@example.com.

Two placeholders to swap: the 2 GB / 90 day backfill numbers and the support address. The conflict-handling paragraph assumes you keep both versions rather than last-write-wins; if your implementation does the latter, that sentence needs rewriting.
